Dutch city of Utrecht to experiment with a universal, unconditional 'basic income'

Headlines in two years:

"Utrecht bankrupt amid towering unemployment"

"Protestors hit the streets in Utrecht as supply of other people's money dries up"

Health; Most of what we’re all stressed out about is money. This stress leads to poor mental health, which leads to poor physical health, both of which lead to medical bills, which lead to even more stress about money! This survival anxiety can be eliminated with a basic income. So people can focus their mental energy on something other than worrying about money.

Crime; When you are less stressed financially you are also less likely to do something drastic and act out violently. Crime is often not the result of bad people but regular people (like you and me) put in bad situations. The odds someone will steal money is greatly reduced if they do not need it.

Ethics; Everybody agrees it’s messed up for Sea World to punish and deprive whales of food to get them to do tricks. But we treat humans the same way. It’s unnecessary and unethical to force people to do tricks to survive when there’s more than enough resources to go around.

Productivity; If people didn’t have to work to survive, you might worry that nothing would get done. Sure some people would leave their work if they had a choice. But that’s good because it opens up a job for someone else who does want it. It frees everyone up to do work that they want to do, work that they find meaningful. Whatever people choose to do: Volunteering, parenting, programming open source software that’s gonna change the world—Productivity would increase because people who like their work are better at it and more efficient.

Fair Wages; If people are dependent on a job for survival, they have to take any job available. They can never negotiate a fair wage. Companies will only offer fair wages when people actually have a choice not to work. Basic income gives everyone that choice.

Efficiency; Western welfare is a complex maze of separate anti-poverty programs. That’s a lot of bureaucratic departments reviewing, rejecting, re-reviewing, then maybe accepting applications and doing the same thing over week after week. What a waste of time and money! Cut out the bureaucracy and just give the money to everyone.

Transparency; 1 basic income program is so simple and efficient that it’s effectively transparent. So there would be less bureaucracy for government to hide behind.

Eliminate poverty
Isn't this what socialism has tried and failed so many times before?
Thomas Paine, author of Common Sense, wanted basic income in the US in 1770

Unlikely.

Unconditional basic income, just like social security systems, are essentially a subsidy for the market because the people who rely on it will not save the money, they will immediately spend it.

Every product is composed of production cost, which eventually breaks down into labor cost and profit margin. Considering this, the basic income, just like any other social security system has a (small) direct payout spread between the companies who sell the commonly bought products and a larger part indirectly distributed between the laborer and their companies who compose the production cost.

It is probably easier to explain with a very simple example.

A fishermen fishes fish with his hands, he fishes 10 hours a day and catches 10 fish per day. There are 10 people who want to eat fish, but only 9 can pay for it (1 Gold). The fishermen sells 9 fish.

Now everybody decides to chip in and give the poor one enough money to buy a fish every day. Now the fishermen sells 10 fish.

Who ended up with what?

The poor guy now got +1 fish Everybody got -0,1 Gold Fishermen got +1 Gold

It was not the poor guy who ends up with the money, it was a fishermen. It is not supporting not working, but rather creates more incentive to work. This is condemning why social security based on the idea that it does not work is utterly pointless. It is redistributing money collectively to incentive's and support businesses, essentially trickle up economy. In oppose to trickle down economy is works (mostly) because the poor person has to spend the money to survive while the rich person (trickle down economy) does not.

Or if you like the more brutal approach.

If you take every unemployed person and send them to the moon into a new founded colony to have never contact with earth again, did you suddenly get rid of unemployment?

No, the lack of consumers will immediately cause people to lose the jobs because too little product gets sold. Unemployment is essentially just statisticly size that described (aside from regular friction that every system has) the necessary amount of subsidize to the local economy. If you pay unemployed people more (up to the cap that they will necessarily spend) you reduce the amount of people who are out of a job because you are changing the necessary multiplier.

You can also cut taxes in the same amount, but only for the bottom bracket or tie it to the requirement to spend the money immediately.

I'm a freelance picture editor for two major German news sites. I work at their newsdesks so when something happens in the world I'll try to find, buy and verify the appropriate pictures for the news. It's a quick paced job, I've worked for a major newspaper which was chilled, now it's online only for me and that's much more fun.
What's your platform? As in, where do you find work? Odesk, Fiverr, or do you just have a website where people can hire you directly?
I'm in the job for around 10 years now. I just know all those people. It really a mouth to mouth thing
Another question for you; what made you decide to go freelance with it? Did you just feel the need to decide your own working hours?

Newspaper went bankrupt lol But the market for picture editors in Germany is really good for freelancers right now. I earn more than before which has to do with the tax code which is quite favorable for me and I just enjoy to be in different places with different people doing different things. I was employed for 2 years out of 10 and I have to say: freelance si much better. You stay sharp when you have to adapt constantly. And the field is so fluid atm with the ever changing legal framework it's great to see how different companies come to different conclusions how to handle stuff.
Do you work in photoshop or any image editing software? Or do you basically just get the pictures and post them as is?

Basic Photoshop but not too much. With journalistic/editorial stuff you have to be very careful not to change the basic message of the picture. We have to crop but also careful not to change the basic configuration of the motive. Otherwise this could happen: http://blogs.reuters.com/gbu/2010/06/07/cropped-photos/
Oh wow that's actually really cool and insightful! It's probably good to not have to spend tons of time editing images since the news tends to move so fast.

The problem is mostly of not with the editing but with old and very badly programmed content management systems. Most news sites are offshots from print magazines/newspapers and they went online 10 or 15 years ago. They bought state of the art software back then and some are still stuck with this crap. It takes ages to get an image into it and crop the right frames for every format which the site is going to deliver. It can take up to 5 Min just to get an image into the system. With the newer systems your down to like 30 sec - 1 min when the picture management system which is connected to the agency stream is fully integrated to the CMS.
Ah I see. Basically some of the news industry is going the way of Government and holding onto ancient technology?

I guess it similar. It's really expensive and complex to migrate an existing site and production system to new one. You can't buy it off the shelf, you have to tailor it specifically for your needs and workflows. So you loose some of your most experienced employees because these are the guys who can analyse your current workflow and work with the company making the CMS/media production system to build a software that suits your needs. Then you have to train all staffers and freelancers and you have to make sure you don't fuck up the migration of the data of the existing site. Especially for news sites, if you screw up the URLs for example Google is going to punish you. It's not uncommon to loose rank and therefore traffic after a relaunch. So you have a very compilcated process which last for big sites between 1 to 2 years, which costs a shitton of money and binds some of your best staff. The situation has to be really painful before you go down that road, especially in a time when most news corps are in a bad situation financially.
What's the pay like? Is it a comfortable warning/are there off seasons etc?

No off seasons. But when everybody else goes on holidays the demand surges. I work over christmas and new years eve and get double the pay and go on vacation after that. If your flexible, having no kids helps, your fine. The pay is ok. Real numbers are not that helpful I guess because of different living costs and taxes in certain countries but I'm above the average compared to other people with humanitas degrees and more in the range of science and technology degrees when they are employed.

So, "Hello, World" is the tried-and-true first program written by new programmers, and old programmers starting a new language.

I'm looking for suggestions on a more advanced default program/project, that one can write fairly quickly (10-60 minutes or so), that is likely to make use of a wide variety of a language's features, and will allow for decent comparison/contrast of of features between languages.

For instance, I will sometimes write a tic-tac-toe game, or a word/letter frequency analyzer, in a new language as I start learning it, to get a hands-on feel for the differences from languages I already know. So, maybe I already answered my own question, but I'd like to hear what other people think might make good projects for this.

One simple idea that I like is writing a little program to open commonly used files instead of manually navigating and double clicking. It touches on basic GUI use (creating a window & some buttons) as well as using built-in OS operations. This obviously doesn't cover a very wide range of features, but still could prove somewhat useful if expanded upon.

It's a great question but there is a caveat to it: what platform are you aiming at?

Which of the following applies:

  • desktop OS application
  • desktop website (non-mobile interface)
  • mobile website (geared specifically at low-bandwidth and small screen)
  • mobile application (native)
  • mobile application (non-native, e.g. uses HTML/CSS/JS instead of Objective C/Java)

Here are my two credits worth of thoughts on each.

On the desktop I'd go for a calculator. It can be as simple as basic arithmetic to more advanced features like graphing output on a formula using a GUI library.

A website, either desktop or mobile, do a blog. Not just any blog, but one written using object-oriented code. Do role-based permissions, repository patterns, events, JSON (or XML) API, handling uploads, etc. Can be done with or without a framework.

Mobile apps I'm not really well versed on a concept that would be great to cover basics of each. For that, someone else will have to chime in.
Similar to tic-tac-toe, writing Blackjack is also a good one. You can make it as simple or complex as you like: start off with just text-based and then create a UI for it.
Found it. Here's what I was looking for ... rosetta code.
Writing a basic infix to postfix converter, or a small calculator. A lot of string manipulation, function modularity, file I/O, basic dictionary/array data structures.
I usually do two things after "Hello, World". First, I check that I can perform simple mathematical operations. Second, I check that I can open files, read from them and write to them.

I usually write a database-backed and/or file system backed to-do list application to learn a new language. Usually, 60 minutes is more than enough. If there's plenty of time, also add user login feature, so there will be different list for different user.
